environment.host_window_alignment: interior host samples selected by contemporaneous Unix timestamps; host/guest offset uncertainty is not measured, so alignment is approximate and not per-request causality
environment.conclusion: Host swap-in and swap-out actually occurred during this serial round. Guest swap is zero; observed service/driver/database cgroup memory events, PSI and major faults are reported separately. These observations cannot identify host paging of a specific guest process or assign individual tail spikes.

metric_definitions.cpu_us_per_correct: service cgroup usage_usec delta between pre-driver launch and post-driver completion, divided by all correct requests including terminal tail; excludes startup and later full-service teardown, driver/observer/PG CPU; complete_lifecycle_accounted=false
metric_definitions.memory_median: cgroup memory.current sampled in arrival window at 1Hz, median of middle60% samples; not RSS, not exact allocation high-water or per-Task memory
metric_definitions.threads: sampled min/max whole-service-cgroup thread count in arrival window; includes workers/runtime support threads
metric_definitions.p99: client-recorded conservative histogram upper edge for scheduled arrival to correct completion, including client queue/dial/write/read/validation; linear10us bins below2.56ms, higher relative bin width<=0.78125%; not an exact sorted percentile
metric_definitions.generator_p99: not recorded: scheduled_to_generated has zero samples in these client reports
metric_definitions.cpu_comparison: single sequential windows; no confidence intervals or stable ranking; different language/runtime semantics remain part of measured implementations

limitations: Not an interleaved seven-window comparison; fixed order, JIT warmup and environmental drift can matter.
No dynamic CPU profiling in this round, so aggregate differences do not identify a runtime hotspot.
Public HTTP bodies validated; Ku uses text/plain while other stacks use application/json variants.
Ku JSON subtree access copies; Rust moves and Go/Node retain references; these are normal API semantics, not identical ownership work.
PG uses same SQL/keys/pool16 without retries or result caching; Ku DISCARD ALL is extra reset work versus other default pools.
Host swap activity does not establish that Ku guest pages were swapped; guest has no swap and cgroup memory/major-fault evidence has a different boundary.
Minor faults can arise from allocation or file mappings and are not swap evidence.
1Hz guest and approximately5s host observations miss subinterval behavior; no claim of zero environment impact.
No process commands, tokens, credentials, user absolute paths or raw process inventories are exported.
